summary: This lecture continues the discussion of Islamic belief (Iman) from Zadul-Ma'ad, focusing on the fourth level of understanding Allah's decree (Qadr). Sheikh Ali Mashhour emphasizes the importance of authentic hadith scholarship and warns against contemporary trends of individuals questioning the authenticity of hadith collections like Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim without proper scholarly credentials. He discusses the difference between fabricated narrations (which are abundant but found only in obscure sources, never in the six major hadith collections) and authentic ones, using an inauthentic story about Jibreel as an example. The lecture explains the four levels of belief in divine decree: knowledge, writing in the Preserved Tablet, will, and creation. Finally, he clarifies the distinction between Allah's legislative will versus his universal will, explaining why evil exists in creation—not for its own sake but for wisdom that can only manifest through it.
suggested_title: The Fourth Level of Divine Decree and Understanding Allah's Creative Will in Islamic Belief
